itemdespawntowhat.command.debug.scene.de: Basic conversion: 1 paper produces 1 prismarine shard.
Fail the height condition and retry, then move the source up 3 blocks: produce 1 shard.
Backoff isolation: purely environmental and under-count rules do not feed the backoff; the natural rule is only waited for and the failure count stays 0.
Convert 1 paper and produce 1 prismarine shard after a 100-tick delay.
Set source age to one tick before platform lifespan: convert at natural expiry.
A stack of 16 paper: one submission, 16 groups, and 16 shards.
Two rules with different due ages: the earlier rule converts first.
A check-locked source and an unlimited-lifetime source: no conversions; both paper remain.
1 check-locked paper merges with 4 plain paper of the same item: the merged pile stays protected, so nothing converts and 5 paper remain.
Reload after the delayed effect is queued: cancel the settlement and effects; produce nothing.
Empty-load baseline, 60 seconds by default.
Conversion load: 1,000 entities and 60 seconds by default; count and duration are configurable.
Heavy preparation load: 1,000 sources with stack 16, a loot table and a conditioned effect that both fail; expects 16,000 paid groups and no output within 60 seconds by default.
Continuous condition failure and retry: 1,000 entities and 60 seconds by default.
Non-converting paper baseline: 1,000 entities and 10 seconds by default; maximum 1,000 source entities.
Paper converts after 5 game seconds: 1,000 entities and 10 seconds by default; maximum 1,000 source entities.
itemdespawntowhat.command.debug.scene.he: Run /idtw debug examples for every functional and benchmark scenario and its expectations.
itemdespawntowhat.command.debug.scene.de: 12 paper, source cost 3: produce 4 prismarine shards.
10 paper, source cost 3: produce 3 prismarine shards and return 1 protected paper.
2 paper cannot pay source cost 3: produce nothing and return both paper.
Priority candidates: all 4 paper select first, producing 4 prismarine shards.
4 independent sources alternate candidates: 2 prismarine shards and 2 gold nuggets.
2 paper: each group produces 1 shard and 2 gold nuggets delayed by 40 ticks; total 2 shards and 4 nuggets.
4 paper with chance 0: pay source costs, produce nothing, and log 4 chance skips.
An all_of + any_of + inverted condition tree converts 1 paper into 1 prismarine shard.
4 paper and 4 emeralds, catalyst cost 1 per group: produce 4 prismarine shards.
4 paper and 2 emeralds: run only 2 groups, produce 2 shards and return 2 paper.
1 paper stack (64) and 64 emeralds; after planning starts the catalyst stack is pushed 4 blocks up: all 64 groups still pay and produce 64 prismarine shards.
2 paper and 3 emeralds, each group needs 2 emeralds present but spends 1: the plan and the pre-group check agree on 2 groups, producing 2 shards and leaving 1 emerald.
64 paper with 20 loot-table effects per group (20 dirt each): the item-capacity check truncates the plan to 51 groups, producing 1020 dirt and returning 13 paper.

26 paper convert in 13 groups: 130 stone pack into 3 stacks, another slot produces a separate stack of 13 stone, and 26 diamond swords arrive across ticks after a 60-tick delay; 30 output entities total.
Fault injection: the first condition check step throws; tracking reschedules and converts the paper on the next tick.
Fault injection: rule reload fails after tracking is established; the old rules and tracking stay effective, and the paper still converts on schedule.
Fault injection: one cancel callback throws while the queued effects are cancelled; the whole batch is still cancelled, the reload succeeds and nothing is produced.
3 paper convert, then reload before the delayed effects fire: one cancel callback throws, the other effects are still cancelled, nothing is produced and no task is left in the scheduler.
Fault injection: effect preparation throws once; tracking reschedules and converts the paper on the next tick.
Fault injection at natural expiry: effect preparation throws; tracking is released and the paper is discarded by vanilla instead of being kept forever.
Reload rules mid-run: the rescan rebuilds tracking in bounded steps and all 16 paper stay tracked.
Reload rules after 64 pending checks are queued: cancellation runs a bounded number per tick, and every paper converts after the rescan without loss.
Five rule reloads over 1,000 entities: each rescan advances in bounded steps and every source stays tracked.
Reload after the delayed effect is queued: the settlement has nothing left to return, so the aborted record is finalised and trimmed immediately; no task is left in the scheduler.
In-session recovery after a settlement step throws: three recovery attempts fail with 20/40-tick backoff, then one alert is logged and the record stays in the ledger for the next startup scan.
A settlement step throws once: the in-session recovery queue delivers the 3 paper, the record completes and the ledger has no pending delivery.
itemdespawntowhat.command.debug.scene.he: /idtw debug run <scene> [seconds]: prepare a functional scenario; default 12 seconds. Tab completes scene names.
/idtw debug bench <scene> [entities] [seconds]: at most 1,000 source entities; empty-load scenarios accept seconds only. See examples for defaults.
Use status, mark <observation>, or stop to control the current scenario. Early stop is INCOMPLETE.
In the IDEA console, filter [IDTW_DEBUG] or run=<id>; compare START parameters, real events, FRAME metrics, and END expected/actual results.
First-load profiling: /idtw debug profile on|off toggles it; reopen the editor to log [IDTW_DEBUG] profile segments for server preparation, delivery, and client refresh.
